nodes.name: Pyrolytic reduction in pure Ar
nodes.procedure: Ni₃(BTC)₂ precursor is pyrolyzed in pure Ar atmosphere with 10°C/min ramp rate. Decomposition begins at 200°C releasing water (O-H at 3490 cm⁻¹, H₂O at 3802 cm⁻¹), CO₂ (C=O at 1745 cm⁻¹), and Ni-O (540 cm⁻¹) from -COO⁻…Ni²⁺ structure. At 250-300°C amorphous Ni-O structure forms. At 300°C C-O (1123 cm⁻¹) appears as Ni²⁺ reduces to Ni⁰. From 300-390°C Ni-O fades as Ni fully reduces and stabilizes with carbon atoms. C-H (3100 cm⁻¹) appears at 300°C, disappears after 30 min at 390°C. Hold at 390°C for 60 min results in 22.6% mass loss and 39.7 wt% carbon content (C_rich-Ni, LC_{0.60}-Ni).

nodes.name: Pyrolytic reduction in 4% H₂/Ar
nodes.procedure: Ni₃(BTC)₂ precursor follows same decomposition/reduction pathway as Ar pyrolysis through 390°C, then holds at 390°C in 4% H₂/Ar atmosphere. Hydrogen acts as lattice carbon scavenger enabling 28.4% total mass loss (vs 22.6% in Ar) producing C_less-Ni with LC_{0.44}-Ni (0.44 C/Ni ratio).

nodes.name: Pyrolytic reduction in 8% H₂/Ar

C_less-Ni (LC_0.44-Ni) can maintain both j_{0,disk} and ECSA better than C_clean-Ni (LC_0.03-Ni) with 89% of j_{0,disk} (61% for C_clean-Ni (LC_0.03-Ni)) and 96% of ECSA (89% for C_clean-Ni (LC_0.03-Ni)) maintained.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples exhibit characteristic peaks of metallic fcc Ni (PDF#04-0850) without phase transformation; higher H2 concentration shows better crystallinity and micro-strain decreases from 3.67% to 0.72%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 2a, although all the samples exhibit characteristic peaks of metallic fcc Ni without any phase transformation (PDF#04-0850), the catalyst obtained in higher H2 concentration shows better crystallinity...

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show nickel nanoparticles separated by thin carbon layer; particle sizes are 3.8 nm for C_rich-Ni, 4.6 nm for C_less-Ni, and 11.8 nm for C_clean-Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was then adopted to probe the structure changes... Specifically, C_rich-Ni have a mean size of 3.8 nm, evidently smaller than that of C_less-Ni (4.6 nm) and C_clean-Ni (11.8 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: C_rich-Ni shows disordered Ni atom arrangement and expanded Ni(111) plane spacing in outer layers; C_less-Ni shows more ordered arrangement with localized expansion; C_clean-Ni shows well crystallinity with homogeneous Ni(111) spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) was further performed to observe the detailed structures of the catalysts. In C_rich-Ni, the arrangement of Ni atoms appears to be disordered... In contrast, the C_clean-Ni shows well crystallinity...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2 XPS shows peaks at 853 eV (Ni0) and 855.5 eV (Ni2+); C_rich-Ni main peak shifted to higher energy (Niδ+ like Ni3C); LC content ratios 0.60, 0.44, 0.03 for C_rich-Ni, C_less-Ni, C_clean-Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectra of Ni2p3/2, the peaks located at 853 eV and 855.5 eV belong to Ni0 and Ni2+, respectively. However... main peak in Crich-Ni is significantly shifted towards higher energy... Quantitative analysis (Table S2) shows that C_rich-Ni (LC0.60-Ni) has the highest C-Ni bonds ratio of 0.60...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows positive shift and stronger white line for C_rich-Ni (LC0.60-Ni) and C_less-Ni (LC0.44-Ni) vs C_clean-Ni (LC0.03-Ni), indicating higher average Ni valence state due to LC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3b presents the X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of the samples at the Ni K-edge. The C_rich-Ni (LC0.60-Ni) and C_less-Ni (LC0.44-Ni) show a positive shift relative to C_clean-Ni (LC0.03-Ni), indicating an increase in the average valence state of Ni...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge EXAFS shows Ni-Ni coordination at ~2.11 Å; C_rich-Ni shows expanded Ni-Ni bond length and Ni-C coordination at 1.47 Å; Ni-C coordination also observed in C_less-Ni confirming residual lattice C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3c presents the Fourier transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS oscillation... A major peak at ∼2.11 Å... is ascribed to the metallic Ni-Ni coordination. It is evident that C_rich-Ni (LC0.60-Ni) shows the expanded Ni-Ni bond length... And coordination of Ni-C at 1.47 Å has been observed in C_rich-Ni...

nodes.characterization_summary: Carbon content decreases from 39.7% (Ar) to 12.6% (8% H2/Ar); 390°C holding stage mass loss 22.6% (Ar) vs 28.4% (4% H2/Ar).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TG results for the obtained catalysts confirm this change of carbon content (Figure S3 and Figure S4). The results show that the carbon content of catalysts decreases from 39.7% (in Ar) to 12.6% (in 8% H2/Ar)...

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function (WF) of Ni increases with LC presence, confirming electron transfer from Ni to C atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) analysis shows that the work function (WF) of Ni increases when the LC presents (Figure 5a and Figure S24), further demonstrates the electron interaction between LC atoms and Ni.
